$$\begin{aligned}\text{Tonnes of concrete} &= 14.4\times 3.52 \\ &= 50.688 \text{ tonnes} \\ &\approx 51 \text{ tonnes (2 significant figures)}\end{aligned}$$

4415.stem: Tom is 25 years old, and likes to keep fit by exercising.

parts.latex:
Use this formula to find his maximum heart rate (bpm).

$$\text{Maximum heart rate} = 220 - \text{age in years}$$

Tom's maximum heart rate is $\underline{\hspace{3cm}}$ bpm.

Tom will get the most benefit from this exercise if his heart rate is between $50\%$ and $85\%$ of his maximum heart rate.

Between what two heart rates should Tom be aiming for to get the most benefit from his exercise?

solutions.latex: $$\begin{aligned} \text{Maximum heart rate} &= 220 - 25 \\ &= 195 \text{ bpm} \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} 50\% \text{ of } 195 &= 97.5 \text{ bpm} \\ 85\% \text{ of } 195 &= 165.75 \text{ bpm} \end{aligned}$$
So Tom should aim for a heart rate between $97.5$ bpm and $165.75$ bpm.
criteria: Provides a correct percentage, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
A plumber charges a call-out fee of \$90 as well as \$2 per minute while working.

Suppose the plumber works for $t$ hours.

Which equation expresses the amount the plumber charges ($\$C$) as a function of time ($t$ hours)?

solutions.latex:
The charge is per minute, so convert the working time to minutes: $t$ hours is $60t$ minutes.

The variable charge is
$$2 \times 60t = 120t$$
Add the call-out fee of \$90:
$$C = 90 + 120t$$
This is option D.

parts.latex:
Ayla wishes to estimate the number of trees on a square block of land measuring 1000 m by 1000 m. She counts the number of trees on a 5 m by 5 m section of the block and finds there are 8 trees.

Based on this, estimate the number of trees on the entire square block of land.

solutions.latex:
The number of trees is proportional to the area, so
$$\dfrac{8}{5 \times 5} = \dfrac{x}{1000 \times 1000}$$
where $x$ is the required number of trees.
$$\therefore\ x = \dfrac{8\,000\,000}{25} = 320\,000$$
criteria: Provides correct area of the block of land, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Leila's car has a fuel consumption of 7.8 L/100 km. The current cost of fuel is \$2.11/L, and Leila spends \$87 to fill up her car tank from empty.

What is the maximum distance Leila can travel with a full tank of fuel?

solutions.latex:
Find the volume of fuel in a full tank.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Volume} &= \dfrac{87}{2.11} \\ &\approx 41.23 \text{ L} \end{aligned}$$
The car uses $7.8$ L per $100$ km.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Distance} &= \dfrac{41.23}{7.8}\times 100 \\ &\approx 529 \text{ km} \end{aligned}$$
This is option B.

4541.stem:
Scarlett lives with her parents and two siblings. Every evening her parents watch television together for 2.5 hours and Scarlett and her siblings are on their devices for 4 hours.

The television consumes 270 watts per hour and each of the children's devices consumes 130 watts per hour.

parts.latex: How much electricity, in kilowatt-hours, is consumed by the household each week?

If the average rate for electricity is \$0.17/kWh and the household receives a 25% discount for paying all of their bills on time, how much does it cost to run the television and children's devices each year?

solutions.latex:
Energy is power times time. Find the Wh used in a week (7 evenings).

Television (one set, 2.5 hours):
$$\text{TV} = 270\times 7\times 2.5 = 4725 \text{ Wh}$$
Devices (3 children, 4 hours):
$$\text{Devices} = 3\times 130\times 7\times 4 = 10\,920 \text{ Wh}$$
Convert to kilowatt-hours by dividing by $1000$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= \dfrac{4725 + 10\,920}{1000} \\ &= 15.645 \text{ kWh} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 15.645 \text{ kWh per week}$$
criteria: Finds the weekly consumption of both the television and the devices, or equivalent merit
Finds the weekly consumption of the television or the devices, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us.

solutions.latex:
There are 52 weeks in a year.
$$\text{Electricity per year} = 15.645\times 52 = 813.54 \text{ kWh}$$
The 25% discount means paying $75\%$ of the cost.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Cost} &= 813.54\times 0.17\times 0.75 \\ &= \$103.73 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Cost} = \$103.73 \text{ per year}$$
criteria: Finds the yearly consumption, or equivalent merit

Find $65\%$ and $85\%$ of the maximum heart rate $193$.

parts.latex: A 4-kilolitre water tank is being emptied at the rate of 5 litres per minute. How long will it take to empty the water tank? Answer in hours and minutes.

solutions.latex:
$4$ kL $= 4000$ L.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Time} &= \dfrac{4000}{5} \\ &= 800 \text{ min} \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} 800 \div 60 &= 13 \cdot \dot{3} \text{ h} \\ &= 13 \text{ h } 20 \text{ min} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 13 \text{ hours } 20 \text{ minutes}$$

parts.latex:
Linus has calculated that it costs \$5.37 per week for the electricity to run his 800-watt washing machine.

The cost of his electricity is 37.29 cents per kWh.

How many hours per week is the washing machine used?

solutions.latex:
Energy used per week equals cost divided by cost per kWh.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Energy} &= \dfrac{5.37}{0.3729} \\ &= 14.4 \text{ kWh} \end{aligned}$$
The machine is 800 W $= 0.8$ kW, and energy $=$ power $\times$ time.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Time} &= \dfrac{14.4}{0.8} \\ &= 18 \text{ hours} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the machine is used for 18 hours per week (option D)}$$

parts.latex:
Water is flowing out of a tap at a rate of 8 mL/second.

What is the equivalent rate of flow?

solutions.latex:
There are 3600 seconds in an hour and 1000 mL in a litre.

$$\begin{aligned} 8 \text{ mL/s} &= 8\times 3600 \text{ mL/hour} \\ &= 28\,800 \text{ mL/hour} \\ &= 28.8 \text{ L/hour} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the equivalent rate is } 28.8 \text{ L/hour (option C)}$$

$$\therefore\ \text{Total fuel cost} = \$151.55$$
criteria: Calculates the amount of fuel used, or equivalent merit

At this speed, how many seconds would it take a wombat to run 150 metres?

solutions.latex:

Approximately how many times faster is the cheetah than the sloth?

Divide the cheetah's speed by the sloth's speed.
$$\dfrac{1733.3}{2.4}\approx 722$$
Hence the answer is B.

The cost of operating the air conditioner to heat the house during winter last year was \$640. There are 92 days in winter.

Find the number of hours, to 1 decimal place, that the air conditioner was used on average per day.

Alternatively, let $h$ be the average hours per day.
$$\begin{aligned} 640 &= 92 \times h \times 0.29 \times 3.2 \\ 640 &= 85.376h \\ h &= \dfrac{640}{85.376} \\ &= 7.49\ldots \\ &\approx 7.5 \text{ hours} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the cost per day, or equivalent merit

6103.stem: A car has a fuel consumption of 13.8 L/100 km.

solutions.latex:
Convert the Calories burned to kJ:

$$\begin{aligned} 1800 \times 4.184 &= 7531.2 \text{ kJ} \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} 8700 - 7531.2 &= 1168.8 \text{ kJ} \end{aligned}$$

solutions.latex:
Substituting into the Harris-Benedict formula, with height $165$ cm:

$$\begin{aligned} \text{BMR} &= 278 + 57.5 \times 63 + 20.9 \times 165 - 28.2 \times 17 \\ &= 6869.6 \text{ kJ/day} \end{aligned}$$

Convert the BMR to kJ per hour:

$$\text{BMR} = \dfrac{7000}{24} = 291\dfrac{2}{3} \text{ kJ/hour}$$

Using the energy formula with PAL $8.6$:

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Energy out} &= 0.5 \times 291\dfrac{2}{3} \times 8.6 \\ &\approx 1254 \text{ kJ} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Converts BMR to kJ/hour, or equivalent merit

Each loop is $2$ km, so the number of full loops is $\dfrac{13.71}{2} \approx 6.9$.

Craig’s target heart rate when exercising is calculated using the following formula:

can_use: Changing the subject of a formula

$$\begin{aligned} \text{time} &= \dfrac{7.0769}{2.5} \\ &\approx 2.8308 \text{ hours} \end{aligned}$$
Convert the decimal part to minutes.

$$0.8308 \times 60 \approx 49.85 \approx 50 \text{ minutes}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{about 2 hours 50 minutes per week.}$$
